page.check_cancelled: The check was cancelled: the counts are partial.

page.ignore.sub: The .mpdignore files: what MPD's update would meet under this folder, the lines that would keep the junk out, and those lines written on your say.
page.ignore.video_title: Glass plays video from the library; with video in use, video containers are counted and never suggested.

Preview shows the lines added, removed and kept before anything is written, and every write can be undone from the Written tab. A line in force from a folder above is edited in that folder: the names under "Lines in force" open it.
page.ignore.placeholder: one pattern per line, as MPD reads it: *.iso, [#]recycle, @eaDir

page.ignore.other_help: Nothing claims these; MPD stats each one and moves on. Tick a suffix to spare the stat with a line; the line matches the suffix as written, since MPD matches case for case.

page.cue.none: No CUE sheet under this folder.
page.cue.each_help: Sheets with findings first. A finding says what MPD does with the sheet as it is; Repair shows what the sheet would be with the repairs it allows, and writes it on your say.

page.tags.sub: Every audio file under this folder read for its tags, what MPD takes of them, and whether a folder shows as one album or several. Read-only; every file is opened, so a large folder takes a while.
page.tags.scope_root_hint: This check walked the whole library. For tag work on music, open the music share and check that folder.
page.tags.repair_help: The audio files of the folder in hand, not the folders under it. The album artist and the date written where MPD reads them, text that is UTF-8 read as Latin-1 decoded, a tag given twice kept once, an ID3v2 tag from ID3v1, and the Album, Album artist and Date every file gets where the files disagree. Each file is shown with its changes before anything is written. DSF and DFF files are read, not written.
page.tags.editor_help: Every audio file of the folder in hand as a grid, one column per field MPD reads. Type in a cell, or set a column for every file at once; an empty cell removes the key. Nothing leaves the page until Preview, which shows every change key by key; the write and the undo are the same as for the repairs.
page.tags.splits: Folders that show as several albums
page.tags.splits_help: Volumio groups an album by Album and AlbumArtist, falling back to Artist. In these folders the files disagree, so the Albums view shows the folder as more than one album, or spreads an album over several.
page.tags.only_first_folders: Only the first {n} folders are listed; the totals count every one.
page.tags.one_album: Every folder under {path} with music in it reads as one album.

page.tags.nothing: Nothing to say about the tags.

page.mb.title: MusicBrainz
page.mb.help: Look up a release for the folder in hand from its album artist, album and track count. Pick one hit, then Preview shows the tags as they would be written file by file through the same path as the editor. A mix or dump that holds several albums is listed with what to do next, not refused. The public MusicBrainz site is used at one request per second unless a local mirror is set on the plugin's settings page.
page.mb.none: No release matched the folder's tags.
page.mb.mixed_guide: Look up needs one album in one folder. This folder holds {n} albums (a mix, a party dump, or an old collection). Each block names the album and the exact library folder those files should move to.
page.mb.mixed_next: Tick Move or Skip in Organise below, Preview and Write the albums you want moved, then open each new album folder and Look up again.
page.mb.pick: Pick a release, then Preview shows the tags as they would be written.

page.playlists.sub: Every m3u, m3u8, pls and xspf under this folder read as MPD reads it, each entry resolved as a load would, and the repairs a playlist allows: its entries rebased to the files on this player, written on your say.

page.playlists.each_help: Playlists with findings first. A finding says what MPD, and Volumio, do with the playlist as it is; Repair shows what it would be with its entries rebased to the files under the folder in hand, and writes it on your say. Discard removes a playlist file you do not want from the library.

A list simply messed up is repaired: an item whose file is gone found again by its name and folders or dropped, a uri in twice kept once, an item without a uri dropped, a file cut short written back with what could be read.

page.findings.none_open: The last check of {path}, {when}: nothing open.
page.findings.about: Every finding of the last check is kept, so the check is not run again to see it. With no code chosen, folders are listed, since a repair is a folder's. A code chip opens a table of every matching finding, twenty at a time, with a path that opens the folder and a dismiss that stays through later checks. Close and the browser's back leave this view, nothing else does, and it reopens where it was.
page.findings.nothing_listed: Nothing listed: nothing open among the codes chosen.
page.findings.dismiss_all_confirm: Dismiss all {n} open findings for {code}? They stay dismissed through later checks.
page.findings.dismiss_folder_confirm: Dismiss {n} open findings in this folder? They stay dismissed through later checks.
page.findings.close_confirm: A preview is open and nothing has been written. Leave the findings?
page.folder.title: Folder name
page.folder.help: Rename the folder in hand from its album or album artist tags, as Artist/Album under the parent tree, or a name you type. The name is made safe for a share. Browse also offers Rename on a folder row. Nothing is written before the preview and Write; the undo gives the name back. A short name with a tilde may show a soft suggestion on the row.
page.folder.rename_title: Rename this folder from its tags or a name you type
page.folder.hint_title: Suggested name from tags; opens Rename
page.folder.need_folder: Open an album folder to rename it here, or use Rename on a folder row above.
page.preview.folder_rename: The folder as it is and as it would be named.
page.names.title: File names and tags
page.names.help: One pattern, either way: the files named from their tags, or the tags read from the file names. The placeholders are the fields of the grid; the text between them is taken as it is. A name is made safe for a share: slashes, colons and the characters Windows refuses become underscores. A sheet or a playlist in the folder that names a renamed file is rewritten with it. Nothing is written before the preview and Write; the undo gives the names back.
page.preview.refs: {n} {n|sheet or playlist|sheets and playlists} naming them rewritten:
page.undo.sub: Every write MPDantic made, newest first. An undo puts the file back as it was, when nothing else has changed it since. Press Update library when you are ready — MPD is told once, and Volumio rebuilds its album list once. Vacuum clears the journal when undo is no longer needed.
page.undo.vacuum_title: Clear every written batch from the journal; Undo for them will no longer be possible
page.undo.vacuum_confirm: Clear {n} {n|written batch|written batches} from the journal? Undo for them will no longer be possible.
page.system.sub: This player, as one block for an issue: what it is, and how its library sits against MPD's output buffer. It names no share, path or credential, only counts. The album query is measured on your say: MPD is asked for every song with every tag, as Volumio's album view asks, and the reply is counted as it streams, never kept; on a large library MPD works for a few seconds. The block is in English, for the maintainers who read it.
page.system.paste: Paste the block into an issue on GitHub; the About tab has the link.
page.system.error: The report could not be read: {error}
page.system.selected: Selected; copy it with Ctrl+C or Cmd+C.
about.intro: Audits and repairs a Volumio player's music library for MPD, one folder at a time or the whole library from its root: what MPD's update meets under a folder and the .mpdignore lines that keep the junk out; CUE sheets read the way MPD reads them, with the repairs a sheet's text allows; the tags the Albums view is built from, read as written and judged by MPD's own rules. Every write is shown whole first, confirmed once, journaled, and undone from the same page; on a network share it goes through a read-write mount made for the write and released after.
about.evo.title: The evo framework
about.evo.text: MPDantic is part of the evo framework, the shared building blocks this ecosystem is built on. Every name beginning with evo is a piece of that framework, direct or derived.
about.evo.scan: Scan the code, or go to evoframework.org.
about.built.title: Built of
about.credit.mpdantic: The plugin, the core and the pages.
about.credit.lofty: The tag reader: every format MPD reads, read as written, in Rust.
about.credit.encoding: The code pages a CUE sheet that is not UTF-8 is read as: the WHATWG tables, in Rust.
about.credit.mpd_by: MPD by Max Kellermann and contributors.
about.credit.mpd: The player daemon whose rules MPDantic follows, read from its source at the version Volumio ships; nothing of it is built in.
about.credit.volumio: The player this is a plugin of.

core.class.system_folder: A folder the NAS or a desktop writes for itself; MPD walks it.
core.class.sidecar: A file a desktop leaves beside the music; MPD tries it by its suffix.
core.class.archive: MPD opens archives and walks inside; an SACD ISO is not ISO9660 and fails.
core.class.video: MPD's ffmpeg decoder claims this suffix; usually video. Audio-only MP4 is normally .m4a.
core.class.ffmpeg_only: Only MPD's ffmpeg decoder claims this suffix: the file is opened and probed at every update, though it is not music.
core.class.audio: A decoder claims it: a song to MPD.
core.class.cue: A CUE sheet: MPD's cue playlist plugin reads it.
core.class.playlist: A playlist: MPD's playlist plugins read it.
core.class.image: Folder art and pictures; never suggested, Volumio shows them.
core.class.other: Nothing claims it: one stat and MPD moves on.
core.cue.utf16: The sheet is UTF-16; MPD reads it as bytes and makes nothing of it.
core.cue.not_utf8: The sheet is not UTF-8 (read here as Latin-1); MPD replaces what does not decode, so the names show mangled.
core.cue.bom_file: A byte-order mark starts the sheet, so MPD does not see the first line ({first} ...); that line is the FILE, so every track is lost
core.cue.bom: A byte-order mark starts the sheet, so MPD does not see the first line ({first} ...)
core.cue.file_no_type: FILE "{name}" has no type, so MPD ignores the line and the tracks after it belong to the file before, or to none.
core.cue.file_not_quoted: The FILE name is not quoted and has a space in it: MPD takes "{name}" as the name and "{kind}" as the type.
core.cue.file_type: FILE type {kind} is not WAVE, FLAC, MP3 or AIFF: MPD drops every track under this FILE.
core.cue.track_before_file: TRACK {nr} comes before any FILE MPD takes: it has no file and is purged.
core.cue.index_not_time: INDEX {nr} {position} is not mm:ss:ff; MPD ignores it.
core.cue.index_frames: INDEX {nr} {position}: {frames} frames in a second of 75; MPD takes it as written.
core.cue.index_not_after: INDEX {nr} {position} is not after the previous track's start; MPD gives that track no end here.
core.cue.track_no_index: TRACK {nr} has no INDEX MPD can read: it starts at zero.
core.cue.no_track: No AUDIO track in the sheet: MPD makes nothing of it.
core.cue.several_files: {n} FILE entries: fine for MPD; Volumio's own browse shows only the first file's tracks.
core.cue.foreign_above: a path above the sheet's folder
core.cuecheck.too_large: The sheet is {bytes} bytes; not read.
core.cuecheck.not_read: The sheet could not be read: {error}
core.cuecheck.missing: FILE "{name}" is not beside the sheet: MPD adds the tracks and purges them at the end of every update.
core.cuecheck.case: FILE "{name}" is not beside the sheet; "{found}" is, in another case: MPD looks the name up exactly and purges the tracks.
core.cuecheck.suffix: FILE "{name}" is not beside the sheet; "{found}" is: MPD purges the tracks.
core.cuecheck.not_decoded: FILE "{name}" is there but no decoder of this MPD claims its suffix: MPD purges the tracks.
core.cuecheck.foreign: FILE "{name}" is {what}: nothing beside the sheet on this player.
core.cuecheck.named_twice: "{name}" is also named by {others}: MPD indexes its tracks twice.
core.cuecheck.index_past_length: The last INDEX in "{name}" is at {at}, past the file's length of {length}: MPD makes a track it cannot play.
core.cuecheck.split_tracks: The sheet names one file and {n} audio files beside it belong to no sheet: the album may be here twice, as an image and as tracks.
core.encoding.not_offered: {label} is not an encoding offered here
core.encoding.replacement_marks: {n} {n|character|characters} could not be read as {encoding}; {n|it shows|each shows} as a replacement mark
core.encoding.read_as: the text read as {encoding} and written as UTF-8
core.encoding.bom_removed: the byte-order mark removed, so MPD sees the first line

core.cuefix.remove: the sheet removed: {why}; the undo puts it back
